quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

33 Questions • Passing Score 27

questions.question: To prepare for dangers ahead, you should:

options.text: Look at the entire road and all sides constantly.
Look straight ahead at all times.
Drive with your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Focus on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and all sides constantly.
questions.explanation: You can handle dangerous situations better by finding problems before you reach them. Look far ahead, but also scan both sides of the road. Do not just stare at the center.

questions.question: If two vehicles reach a four-way stop at the same time:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must let the vehicle on the right go first.
The vehicle on the right must let the vehicle on the left go first.
Drivers must use hand signals to talk to each other.
One driver should go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must let the vehicle on the right go first.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles go in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the one on the left must yield to the one on the right.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered crossing gates.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red lights and gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop when a flagger, stop sign, gates, or flashing lights tell you to. Not all crossings have these safety devices. It is against the law to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: On a freeway, if you miss your exit, you should:

options.text: Turn quickly from your lane.
Stop and back up.
Keep going until the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep going until the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, do not back up. Go to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around. Backing up on a freeway shoulder is illegal.

questions.question: On a two-lane road without bike lanes, how should you safely pass a cyclist going the same direction?

options.text: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass with plenty of space.
Keep driving straight. The cyclist must get out of your way.
Wait until you reach a traffic light or stop sign to pass.
Honk to let the cyclist know you are coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass with plenty of space.
questions.explanation: Pass a cyclist like you would any other vehicle. Leave at least 3 feet of space, or 5 feet on faster roads or with groups of cyclists. Do not honk suddenly, as it may startle them and cause a crash.

questions.question: You may cross a dashed white line:

options.text: Any time.
Only during the day.
When it is safe to change lanes.
Only when passing a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes going the same direction. You may cross them to pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, the safest way is to:

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive faster than other vehicles.
Drive slower than other vehicles.
Drive at the same speed as other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as other traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other cars. Always drive with the flow of traffic, but within the speed limit.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Flagger ahead.
Lane ends.
Turn right or go straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about road conditions and hazards ahead. This sign warns you of an upcoming intersection.

questions.question: You should use your horn when:

options.text: You are driving through an intersection.
You are passing a cyclist.
You see a child about to run into the street.
You are parallel parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: You see a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. For example, honk if a child starts running into the street in front of you.

questions.question: ____ greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity.

options.text: High speeds
Slow speeds
Driving at night
Driving uphill

questions.correctAnswerText: High speeds
questions.explanation: High speeds greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity. The faster you drive, the harder your vehicle hits if there is a collision.

questions.question: What should you do if traffic signals are not working due to a power outage?

options.text: Park your vehicle off the road and wait for power to be restored.
Use hand signals to show other drivers what you plan to do.
Turn on your hazard lights and drive through without stopping.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection like a four-way stop sign.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection like a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers the same way you would at a four-way stop. When it is your turn, go through carefully.

questions.question: When driving in an area where children are playing, what should you expect?

options.text: They know when it is safe to cross the street.
They will stop at the curb before crossing.
They may run in front of your vehicle without looking.
They will not cross unless an adult is with them.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may run in front of your vehicle without looking.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be extra careful around children. Children may not understand danger and could run into the street without looking.

questions.question: How can you avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before you turn or change lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving to check your blind spot. Do not rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are also approaching.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and stop only if you need to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop, give the right-of-way to other traffic, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: These parking spaces are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.
A roundabout is ahead.
Traffic in this lane must turn in the direction of the arrow.
This lane is reserved for buses and vehicles with multiple passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: These parking spaces are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that parking spaces are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: When turning left, you have the right-of-way with which traffic signal?

options.text: A solid green light
A flashing yellow light
A green arrow pointing left
A flashing red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A green arrow pointing left
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go in the direction the arrow points. Other traffic must stop for you to make your turn.

questions.question: What happens if a bicyclist breaks traffic laws?

options.text: They do not have to follow traffic laws.
They can receive a ticket.
They will always get a warning from police.
Their bicycle will be taken away.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can receive a ticket.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and duties as car drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A steep hill is ahead.
You must turn left ahead.
Do not enter.
A four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A four-way intersection is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a four-way intersection is coming up.

questions.question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?

options.text: Drive slowly so cars and pedestrians have time to get out of your way.
Honk your horn so others know to move.
Stop and only go when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
Ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and only go when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the road from a driveway. Yield to any vehicles or pedestrians. You must stop before crossing the sidewalk. Not stopping is against the law.

questions.question: If you are driving slowly and traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Drive even slower.
Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Do not let other cars pass.
Use your four-way hazard lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic can be dangerous. On a two-way road, if traffic is backing up behind you, you must pull off the road and let other vehicles pass. Only drive slowly when road conditions require it.

questions.question: When you see a red traffic light, you must:

options.text: Stop at the stop line.
Stop before entering any crosswalk.
Stop before entering the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means stop before entering the intersection. You must also stop at any stop line and before entering any crosswalk.

questions.question: If another driver cannot see you in their blind spot, you should:

options.text: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
Keep a steady pace.
Stay in the driver's blind spot.
Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not drive in another driver's blind spot. Move ahead or drop back so the other driver can see you.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes traveling in the same direction. Broken white lines can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: When must you yield for emergency vehicles?

options.text: Under no circumstances.
When you see a flashing red or blue light or hear a siren.
Only when other vehicles yield.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a flashing red or blue light or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any emergency vehicle using a siren or flashing lights.

questions.question: Why must you use extra caution near a pedestrian with a white cane?

options.text: He or she is deaf.
He or she is a police officer.
He or she is blind.
He or she has poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: He or she is blind.
questions.explanation: A white cane means the pedestrian is blind. Slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be ready to stop to avoid hitting them.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, what should you always do?

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing train tracks. Always obey signs and traffic signals. Trains share the road with cars and bicycles.

questions.question: To avoid sudden braking or turning, how far ahead should you look?

options.text: Two seconds ahead of your vehicle.
Four seconds ahead of your vehicle.
10 seconds ahead of your vehicle.
15 seconds ahead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: 10 seconds ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Look at least 10 seconds ahead to avoid sudden braking or turning. This helps you drive safely and keep traffic moving smoothly.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.
Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
Allow the motorcycle to use only half of a lane.
Pass using the same lane as the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle has the same road rights as any other vehicle and needs a full lane. Motorcycles need room to move safely, even if it looks like they could share a lane.

questions.question: Which of these increases the risk of a crash due to distraction?

options.text: CD player
Radio
Cell phone
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Cell phones, radios, and CD players can all distract you and increase crash risk.

questions.question: Your stopping distance increases when you stop on:

options.text: A wet or icy road.
Paved highways.
At night.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A wet or icy road.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance increases on wet or icy roads. It also increases on loose gravel or stones.

questions.question: A green arrow and a red light together mean that:

options.text: You may only drive straight ahead.
You may drive only in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light before moving in any direction.
All vehicles must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drive only in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction the arrow points, and only if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: Before making a right turn, your car should be:

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when you start to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Move as far to the right side of the road as possible before turning right. Do not cross other lanes of traffic to make your turn.

questions.question: You cannot pass on either side of a ____ centerline.

options.text: Combination solid and broken yellow
Single broken yellow
Double solid yellow
Single broken white

questions.correctAnswerText: Double solid yellow
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line down the center of the road means no traffic from either direction can cross it to pass other vehicles.
